reviews.comment: Professor Bierman is awesome. He teaches the class how a traditional law school class would be taught; by briefing cases and having in depth convos. Tests are all free response, but he gives a lot of extra credit on the tests and gives great feedback. Genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed.

Love Professor Bierman. His approach is old school and he's not super adept at Canvas, but he is very passionate about what he teaches and wants to help us succeed. Class is not particularly difficult either. Would highly recommend.

Professor Bierman is such a sweet guy and is extremely knowledgeable about his subject. He's pretty outdated, so expect little to no use of Canvas and written exams. Not particularly difficult though, just a little disorganized. Excellent communication and feedback!

One of the best professors I've had at mays
There's a lot of reading during the first half of the semester, but he curves the quizzes heavily and the exams, especially 2&3 are easy, so there is no reason to opt for the grade contract. The first half is tough, but once you get through the first paper it gets a lot easier.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Bierman was an amazing professor. He offers definitional grading where you can get a B so long as you participate and attend. The only requirements are that you do 2 presentations with 2 long essays. Otherwise you can choose to do pop quizzes and the tests as well and earn up to an A. He was very caring and had engaging lectures.

Professor Bierman is very knowledgeable and passionate about Labor Law. He is very fair and lenient and cares about his students. He made this course interesting by keeping the class engaged during lectures and providing funny examples. We had 2 tests and a final group presentation and paper.
An excellent professor who's passionate about his subject and class. Extremely knowledgeable. LOTS of reading and no extra credit opportunities.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Bierman is a really nice professor. He is very passionate about Paradoxes in the business industry and makes the class very interesting and stimulating. The grade contract is such a nice bonus because it takes the stress off of your shoulders for worrying about your grade. Overall grate professor!
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Bierman is my favorite professor throughout my four years at Mays. His dedication to his students is clear and his class is really interesting. He asks for feedback regularly and implements it. The material is intrinsically difficult, but he makes it manageable. He's also been personally involved in some cool cases.

This class has a lot of material to cover and the only grades you are given are from the 3 exams. This makes it extremely difficult to make an A in the class. 4.0 is pointless, Bierman told us that they dont cover his material the way he likes. The best advice I have is to read his textbook cover to cover, read all of the court cases, and do his EC
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: There are three tests that are 100 points each and that is all your grade is based on. He offers at least three extra credit assignments that are worth a total of 10 points. He does curve generously. I think going to the class is most important to get a good grade. Reading the book before lecture helps you understand what he's talking about.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: Bierman is super enthusiastic and knowledgeable and from the beginning said that he wanted everyone to do well and pass the class. Gives generous curves on tests and multiple extra credit opportunities to help your grade. Most questions are from in-class lecture but the book is good for background. HIGHLY recommend!
reviews.ratingTags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Amazing and super knowledgeable teacher. Kinda goofy, but he really cares about feedback and making sure everyone understands the subject. 3 Exams and 4 extra credit opportunities, he's more than flexible about curving. Textbook use is minimal, but is really beneficial to read after his lectures (don't buy the online one). Definitely take him.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very funny & loved him as a professor. I definitely recommend taking him if you can. The tests are very much based on his lectures but reading the book is recommended since he wrote some of it. He tries to keep the class relevant by incorporating new court cases into the lessons and gives extra credit.

Professor Bierman's tests are 95% based off of his lectures with a little bit from the book. He offers extra credit on every test that takes about 10 minutes max and is pretty much graded on completion. He cares so much about his students, I highly recommend taking him. He takes feedback seriously and wants everyone to do well in his class.

Great class & very interesting. I was worried coming in to it because I had heard it was a weed out class, but all you need to do is read the book, show up to class, and study what he talks about in his powerpoints and you'll be fine. He also gives extra credit which is always good.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Bierman is a nice guy, just not the best prof. He has trouble staying on track during lectures and makes it difficult to understand what is important to know. He says to not worry about knowing the textbook, then finishes almost every powerpoint slide by saying "Don't worry this is all in your book".
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tests are theoretically based so make sure you know your stuff. Gives great curves like 19pts. Do the extra credit for 3pts on each test it can make the difference. He wrote part of the book so you need to get it. Lectures aren't that bad, tries to make them interesting. Also tests more off lectures than the book, but the book helps you understand.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--LECTURE HEAVY
